title: Exposure and contamination response
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate exposure and contamination response

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Stop the task when encountering unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure. Keep others away from the hazard where safe and follow site emergency arrangements. Do not handle sharps or biological material without the required authorisation, training and equipment. For an exposure, follow the relevant first-aid instructions and SDS, seek medical assistance when indicated and report promptly using the workplace incident pathway. Avoid making medical judgments or attempting an untrained clean-up. Record what happened, location, time, immediate controls and who was notified, while protecting personal information.

instruction.heading: Learning focus
instruction.body: Respond to unexpected exposure or contamination. Stop the task when encountering unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure. Keep others away from the hazard where safe and follow site emergency arrangements. Do not handle sharps or biological material without the required authorisation, training and equipment. For an exposure, follow the relevant first-aid instructions and SDS, seek medical assistance when indicated and report promptly using the workplace incident pathway. Avoid making medical judgments or attempting an untrained clean-up. Record what happened, location, time, immediate controls and who was notified, while protecting personal information.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace scenario
instruction.body: A cleaner finds a needle beneath a bin liner. They stop, leave the needle untouched, secure the area as permitted and request an authorised sharps response.

instruction.heading: Guided practice
instruction.body: Role-play a discovery and escalation scenario, demonstrating stop-work, isolation, factual incident reporting and appropriate resumption only after clearance.

instruction.heading: Quality and safety checks
instruction.body: Before signing off, confirm that the method matches the authorised site scope and current product labels, that no uncontrolled hazard remains, and that evidence is factual and privacy-safe.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Stop the task on finding unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure.
Leave any unknown sharp untouched. Do not handle sharps or biological material without the required authorisation, training and equipment.
Keep others away from the hazard where it is safe to do so, and secure the area as permitted.
Follow the site emergency arrangements. For an exposure, follow the first-aid instructions on the product's safety data sheet.
Seek medical assistance when it is indicated. Do not make medical judgments.
Report the event promptly through the workplace incident pathway. Do not attempt an untrained clean-up.
Record what happened, the location, the time, the immediate controls and who was notified, protecting personal information.
Resume only after clearance, and before sign-off confirm that the method matches the authorised scope and that no uncontrolled hazard remains.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The task stops when unknown sharps, bodily fluids or uncontrolled splashes are found.
Sharps and biological material are not handled without the required authorisation, training and equipment.
First-aid instructions and the SDS are followed for an exposure, and medical help is sought when indicated.
The incident is reported promptly and recorded with location, time and immediate actions.
summary: The cleaner stops the task on finding unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure.
Sharps and biological material are handled only with the required authorisation, training and equipment, and others are kept away where that is safe.
An exposure is reported promptly through the workplace incident pathway, and medical judgments are left to qualified people.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be confirmed before handling a sharp or biological material after an exposure?
options: That the sharp can be picked up with bare hands if it is small and the sharps bin is then closed
That the bin liner is opened to see what is inside and its contents are emptied on the floor
That any sharps or biological material is handled only with the required authorisation, training and equipment
That the client has been told about the find first and the client has signed a form about it

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when an unknown sharp is found during a clean?
options: Pick the needle up with tongs and place it in the general waste bin today
Keep working around it carefully and tell the next person later on the day
Wrap it in a cloth and put it in the bin with the rest of the rubbish
Stop, leave the hazard untouched, keep others away, and request an authorised response

options: A client asking for a quote
